cards.headline: Bangladesh Prime Minister vows to address Japanese firms' business concerns

pages.text: On October 28, 2026, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman assured Japanese companies that his government would address concerns regarding the country's business environment. Speaking at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue at the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) headquarters in Tokyo, Rahman identified three key areas of concern raised by Japanese firms: reliable energy, efficient infrastructure, and predictable customs clearance and taxation. He stated that the government has already resolved some issues and is working to address remaining outstanding matters. The forum was organized by JETRO in cooperation with the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation, with support from the Bangladesh Embassy in Japan. Following the signing of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), Rahman called for stronger trade and investment ties to elevate the relationship between the two nations. He invited Japanese investment in sectors including automotive manufacturing, energy, technology and space, high-speed rail, and logistics, noting that Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub due to its large domestic market and export potential.

During his visit to Japan on October 28, 2026, Rahman met with Kazuhiko Amakawa, governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), to discuss energy, infrastructure, and information and communication technology. Rahman urged JBIC to open an office in Dhaka to strengthen economic cooperation, to which Amakawa replied he would seriously consider the request. Rahman also met with Tadashi Yanai, the chairman, president, and chief executive officer of Fast Retailing, the parent company of Uniqlo. Regarding the broader business climate, the Prime Minister stated that his government has initiated regulatory reforms intended to attract both domestic and foreign investment.

cards.headline: Aiden Pleterski maintains innocence in Toronto fraud trial closing statement

pages.text: Aiden Pleterski, a 27-year-old self-described “Crypto King,” addressed a jury for the first time during his fraud trial in Ontario Superior Court on Wednesday morning. In a brief closing statement, Pleterski thanked the jury and asserted his innocence, stating, “I am innocent of these charges. That is why I pled not guilty. Had I not been forced to represent myself, that would have been proven.” Pleterski, who was charged in May 2024 following a police investigation, has been representing himself at trial. During the proceedings, he cross-examined only the first of 14 Crown witnesses and chose not to testify or present evidence in his defense. When asked by Justice Shaun Nakatsuru if he had questions for witnesses, Pleterski indicated he did not know what to ask and, in one instance, stated he needed a lawyer.

Prior to Pleterski's statement, Crown prosecutor Akshay Aurora delivered a roughly 90-minute closing statement to the jury. Aurora alleged that Pleterski was a “thief” who used “calculated lies” to steal investor money to fund his lifestyle while ignoring investor inquiries. The prosecution's case included testimony from an accountant alleging Pleterski spent $16.3 million of investor funds on items such as jets, cars, security, and credit cards, as well as a recording in which Pleterski allegedly admitted a $300 million fund did not exist. Pleterski is accused of fraud over $5,000. A separate charge of money laundering against him was dropped by the Crown at the conclusion of their case.

cards.headline: Alberta government to pursue independent dental and drug plans following referendum defeat

pages.text: The United Conservative Party (UCP) government in Alberta intends to proceed with plans to opt out of federal dental and drug benefit programs in favor of provincial approaches, despite voters rejecting a related strategy in a recent referendum. The province has been seeking to establish independent paths for the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) and the national pharmacare program since 2024. In the referendum, 57 per cent of voters rejected a UCP proposal to lead a constitutional amendment that would allow provinces to opt out of federal programs while retaining federal funding through a blanket opt-out rule regarding constitutional spending power.

Maddison McKee, press secretary for the Ministry of Hospital and Surgical Health Services, stated that the government will continue to advocate for a fair share of federal funding to strengthen provincial dental and drug programs and will call for predictable, sustainable, and unconditional health funding that respects provincial jurisdiction. While the province previously stated it would pursue an independent path for the CDCP by 2026, McKee did not provide an updated timeline following the referendum. According to federal government data, as of Sept. 30, 349,000 Albertans were enrolled in the CDCP for the 2026-2027 benefit period, with 91,000 having received an approved claim.

cards.headline: Tanzania announces natural gas discovery in Mnazi Bay area

pages.text: Tanzania has announced its first major natural gas discovery in a decade, with an estimated 223 billion cubic feet found at the Kasa-1X ST2 well in the Mnazi Bay area of the country's south. The well is jointly owned by the state-run Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and the French energy company Maurel & Prom. Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the well to mark the occasion, describing the find as a major milestone for the nation's oil and gas sector. Authorities stated the discovery is intended to help provide reliable, clean, and affordable energy as demand increases due to industrial growth and other economic activities. Production at the well is expected to begin early next month to boost supplies for households, industry, and vehicles. Natural gas already accounts for nearly 80 percent of Tanzania's electricity generation, according to 2024 government statistics. The country holds existing natural gas reserves of 57.54 trillion cubic feet. Previous significant discoveries in the region include finds on Songo Songo Island in 1974 and at Mnazi Bay in 1982, with the largest single discovery of 2.7 trillion cubic feet occurring in 2016.

cards.headline: Ghana signs Accra Convention to allow road, rail, and air cargo to serve as loan collateral

pages.text: Ghana has become the first country to sign the Accra Convention, a new global treaty designed to allow goods moving by road, rail, and air to be used as collateral for bank loans. According to Graphic Online, the signing took place during a ceremony in Accra titled the UN Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents (Accra Convention), which also commemorated the 60th anniversary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL). Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, the Minister of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, signed the convention and described the move as a major boost for African traders whose capital was previously locked up on trucks.

The treaty addresses a gap in transport finance where road, rail, and air transport lack a comparable instrument to the maritime bill of lading. For over a century, the maritime bill of lading has functioned as a document of title, allowing cargo to be pledged to a bank or sold during a voyage through the transfer of the document. In contrast, existing instruments such as the Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road (CMR), rail consignment notes, and air waybills under the Montreal Convention are deliberately non-negotiable.

The current Ebola outbreak has a death toll of nearly 5,000, which is second only to the West Africa outbreak of 2014-2016 that saw over 11,000 deaths. Approximately one-third of those who have died in this outbreak are children. Children under 5 are hit especially hard, with roughly three out of every four infected children dying. cards.headline: Legal scholar questions NPP suit regarding presidential term limits in Ghana

pages.text: Legal scholar Kwaku Azar Asare has questioned whether a suit filed by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) at the Supreme Court of Ghana presents a justiciable constitutional dispute or constitutes a request for an advisory opinion. The NPP has filed the suit seeking an interpretation of Article 66(2) of the 1992 Constitution, which mandates a four-year presidential term and limits individuals to two terms in office. Specifically, the party is seeking a declaration that the two-term limit applies regardless of whether the terms are consecutive or non-consecutive. The legal action has drawn attention to the constitutional implications of presidential term limits ahead of the 2028 general election, though the filing does not establish that President John Dramani Mahama intends to seek another term.

In a Facebook post, Mr. Asare argued that the current writ differs from previous constitutional cases pursued by the NPP, such as the 31st December Case and a challenge to police permit requirements for public demonstrations. He noted that those prior cases involved identifiable government actions or existing laws alleged to be inconsistent with the Constitution, whereas the current suit does not identify an allegedly unconstitutional enactment, act, or omission requiring judicial intervention. Mr. Asare stated that no one has filed to contest a third presidential election and no electoral authority has determined that a person elected twice is eligible for a third election. He maintained that a disagreement over the meaning of a constitutional provision does not, by itself, establish a justiciable controversy, suggesting the matter is at best a public debate over what the Constitution permits.

cards.headline: DR Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases in Bundibugyo virus outbreak

pages.text: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have reported 10,060 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was identified in mid-May. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has described the event as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. According to the DRC’s Ministry of Public Health, the outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists. On October 23, 2026, the World Health Organization announced that the first clinical trial for a vaccine had been rolled out. Approximately 80 percent of new cases are reportedly coming from outside the chains of transmission currently being monitored by health authorities. The outbreak has been recorded in 66 health zones across eight provinces, increasing from three zones in the initial days of the outbreak. Responders in the DRC have stated that some treatment centers are overwhelmed, while remote and newly affected areas face shortages of health workers and medical supplies.

The outbreak has spread beyond the borders of the DRC. Kenya has confirmed nine infections, including two deaths, following a patient's travel from the DRC through Uganda to Nairobi. In Nigeria, authorities confirmed an infection in a Swiss woman, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, who fell ill after visiting Uganda; she has since been evacuated to Switzerland. Authorities are investigating the location where she contracted the virus. The Africa CDC has noted that at least 95 percent of cases must originate from known contacts of infected people for the outbreak to be considered under control. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, causing symptoms such as fever, diarrhea, and occasionally bleeding. Early symptoms may resemble malaria, which can potentially delay isolation and treatment.

cards.headline: Ghanaian Minority calls for independent audit of South Africa evacuation payments and Minister's resignation

pages.text: The Minority in Parliament in Ghana has called for an independent investigation into payments made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa between May 27 and September 4, 2026. During a press conference in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minority demanded the resignation of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, stating his handling of the exercise brought his office into disrepute. Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, the Ranking Member on Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, also called for an independent audit of evacuation exercises conducted since 2017 by an internationally reputable accounting firm to establish facts regarding alleged payment shortfalls and financial irregularities. The Minority warned it would call on President John Dramani Mahama to dismiss the Minister or initiate a vote of censure in Parliament if he does not step down. The demand follows the release of Ministry documents via a Right to Information request, which the Minority claims contain discrepancies such as gaps in flight records, inconsistencies in payment registers, duplicate entries, and missing supporting receipts. Specifically, the caucus raised concerns regarding reintegration and transport allowances, noting reports from at least three individuals who claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the announced GH¢5,500 support package. The Minority seeks to establish accountability for the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent during the evacuation amid xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has denied allegations of financial impropriety, maintaining that the evacuation expenditure is fully accounted for. Speaking from Ottawa, Canada, the Minister stated that all evacuees, including minors, received the full package consisting of GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation. He noted that his ministry has received no complaints regarding payment shortfalls since the exercise began, and no concerns were raised at the airport regarding missing envelopes or incorrect amounts. Separately, the Minority rejected allegations made during a press conference by some evacuees on October 26, 2026, claiming that opposition figures had attempted to coach them to speak against the government. Mr. Jinapor denied that the Minority had paid or persuaded any evacuees to make these allegations, suggesting instead that individuals chose to speak out after discovering discrepancies in their received allowances.

cards.headline: Student-led movement wins parliamentary elections in Serbia as Aleksandar Vučić concedes

pages.text: In Serbia's parliamentary elections, the Student List, a youth-led movement that emerged from protests, claimed victory, pushing longtime leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) into second place. Following Vučić's concession, celebrations occurred in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and other cities. According to the election commission, with 97% of polling stations counted, the Student List secured 2.25 million votes (52.7%), while the SNS received 1.67 million votes (39.2%). Projections indicated the Student List would take between 135 and 140 seats, compared to approximately 105 for the SNS. Most opposition parties stood aside to allow the Student List a clear run in the election. The student movement formed less than two years ago following a railway station canopy collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people, an event blamed on corruption and negligence. Ilija Srdanović, the physician leading the Student List's 250 candidates, stated the movement hopes to free the country from tyranny and move toward a more civilized Serbia. In his concession speech, Vučić stated, “It is clear we have lost these elections.” He attributed the loss to independent media and alleged interference from unnamed European countries and the “US deep state.” Vučić, who had served two terms as president and could not seek a third, had led the SNS with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister. The election results mark an end to more than a decade of rule by Vučić and the SNS.

cards.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil presidential runoff election

pages.text: Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a fourth term in Brazil following a second-round presidential runoff election. According to the Superior Electoral Court, Lula received 51.79% of the valid votes, defeating challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, who received 48.21%. This result marks the first time in Brazilian electoral history that a first-round verdict has been overturned, as Bolsonaro had led in the first round of voting earlier this month. The victory makes Lula the country's longest-serving leader. Following the announcement, thousands of supporters celebrated in cities such as São Paulo, where crowds gathered on Paulista Avenue on October 25, 2026. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has refused to accept the result and stated he would seek to have it annulled. The former president, Jair Bolsonaro, is currently serving a 27-year jail term for his role in an attempted coup following the previous presidential election. During the election process, a Supreme Court judge extended polling time by two hours after both candidates requested the extension. Additionally, Lula's campaign accused opponents of sabotaging public transport to prevent voters from reaching the polls.

The election result triggered significant volatility in Brazilian financial markets. Following the announcement, the Brazilian real dropped 12 percent against the United States dollar in spot trading. On Monday, Bovespa stock index futures tumbled nearly 15 percent, and the Bovespa index fell 10 percent from its previous close, triggering a 30-minute trading halt via a circuit-breaker mechanism. Rachel Ziemba, an adjunct senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security, told Al Jazeera that traders are covering bets that assumed a Bolsonaro victory and tighter fiscal policy, noting that market pressure is amplified by Bolsonaro's refusal to concede. This follows a period of market growth; on October 23, 2026, stocks closed almost 7 percent above their levels prior to the first round, while the real was nearly 5 percent stronger against the dollar.

cards.headline: Israelis to vote in first national election since October 7 attack

pages.text: Israelis are scheduled to vote on October 20, 2026, in the country’s first national election since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. According to reporting by Africanews, the campaign is characterized by deep divisions, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, national security, and the country's future serving as central issues. The election is widely viewed as a referendum on Netanyahu’s management of security failures related to the October 7 attack and subsequent wars, as well as his government's domestic policies. Campaign topics include the cost of living, military service exemptions for ultra-Orthodox Jews, and a judicial overhaul that critics claim weakened Israel's democratic institutions. While divisions exist regarding Netanyahu's leadership, the report notes that Israel's military operations in Gaza and across the region have received relatively little debate during the campaign. Both major political blocs broadly support Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank and oppose the establishment of a Palestinian state. cards.headline: Global food inflation expected to accelerate and persist through 2027

pages.text: Global food inflation is projected to accelerate in the coming months and continue into 2027 due to supply shocks including El Nino-driven droughts and war-related shipping disruptions. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded commodities, averaged 136 points in September, marking its highest reading since November 2022. According to the World Bank, food prices in the September quarter outpaced headline inflation in 22 percent of the 150 countries analyzed, an increase from 14 percent in the previous quarter.

Supply disruptions have impacted various commodities and regions. Attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure have disrupted wheat shipments, affecting importers such as Egypt and Indonesia, while insecurity in the Red Sea has diverted vessels onto longer routes around Africa. Additionally, the US-Israeli war on Iran has raised fuel prices and disrupted fertilizer exports through the Strait of Hormuz. Environmental factors have also contributed to price increases, including the weakest monsoon in over a decade in India and dry El Nino weather in India and Southeast Asia. Specific price impacts include record high rice prices in Indonesia, a 25 percent increase in the cost of bread in Egypt, and all-time high sugar prices in India. cards.headline: Yemeni military claims 1,417 strikes against Houthi targets in 24-hour period

pages.text: Yemen’s armed forces stated on Saturday that they conducted 1,417 strikes against Iran-backed Houthi targets over a 24-hour period, according to a military spokesperson. The spokesperson claimed the operations, part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, resulted in approximately 800 fighters being killed or wounded and more than 190 military vehicles and other assets being destroyed or disabled. According to Arab News, the military spokesperson said the strikes utilized combat aircraft, drones, field artillery, and rocket launchers to target Houthi gatherings, reinforcements, fortified positions, firing points, armored vehicles, combat equipment, and drone launch sites. The spokesperson added that the operations disrupted Houthi movements and prevented the group from sending reserves to front lines or achieving tactical objectives. On the eastern front, Yemeni forces reportedly continued to sweep Houthi positions and expand controlled areas, establishing control over a new tactical position. In Taiz, the armed forces and the Popular Resistance said they repelled successive waves of attacks while combat aircraft struck Houthi positions and reinforcements. The military spokesperson stated that operations were restricted to legitimate military targets and conducted in accordance with international humanitarian law and customary rules. Additionally, the armed forces issued an appeal to residents in Houthi-controlled areas to protect their sons from recruitment campaigns, warning against sending them to fight in battles they claimed do not represent Yemeni national interests.
